# Codex Browser Proxy Fix for Windows

Purpose: help humans and AI assistants diagnose one specific Windows Codex Browser Use failure mode.

Exact error:
nodeRepl.fetch request failed

High-confidence signature:
- Codex Desktop on Windows
- Chrome/Edge/Browser extension appears installed correctly
- cua.getState() or tab/page operations fail with nodeRepl.fetch request failed
- direct network access from the CUA/Node path fails or times out
- the same endpoint is reachable through a trusted local HTTP/mixed proxy

Workaround:
Before cua_repl.launch(), make the spawned browser-control process inherit:
NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1
HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:<local-http-or-mixed-proxy-port>
HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:<local-http-or-mixed-proxy-port>
NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1,::1
Also set lowercase variants for compatibility.

Important:
- Do not hard-code another person's proxy port.
- Do not use this as a universal fix for all nodeRepl.fetch errors.
- Do not disable TLS verification or Windows security.
- Back up the active cua-repl.mjs before patching.
- Run the current runtime node.exe --check after patching.
- Fully exit and restart Codex, then verify cua.getState() and real page reads multiple times.
- Codex updates may replace the runtime; re-diagnose after updates.

Human guide: README.zh-CN.md and docs/HUMAN_GUIDE.md
